### Burning the Wick or Burning the Oil?
Author: Jeff Schreve
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/fromhisheart/from-his-heart-week-of-october-14.html
Passage: Zechariah 4:6
Points:
- Attempting to do God's work through self-reliance inevitably leads to exhaustion and burnout.
- Scripture uses oil as a picture of the Holy Spirit, providing continuous energy without self-destruction.
- Believers are invited to exchange the strain of human effort for the supernatural strength of Christ.
- Daily surrender of one's own will allows the Holy Spirit to work effectively through us.

### The Master Builder
Author: Truth For Life (adapted by Alistair Begg from C. H. Spurgeon)
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-november-26-2020.html
Passage: Zechariah 4:10
Points:
- Believers should never look down on small beginnings, because the Lord faithfully finishes His work.
- The plumb line held by Zerubbabel points to Jesus Christ as the true Master Builder of the church.
- Christ examines all spiritual construction with careful judgment rather than hasty speed.
- Any work not aligned with Christ must fall, but His chosen temple will reach glorious completion.

### Meeting God in the Mystery of the Mundane
Author: Tiya Thomas-Alexander
Site: The Gospel Coalition | India
URL: https://in.thegospelcoalition.org/article/meeting-god-in-the-mystery-of-the-mundane/
Passage: Zechariah 4:10
Points:
- Human nature naturally craves glamorous achievements while overlooking the value of ordinary maintenance.
- God encouraged Zerubbabel after long, grueling delays by affirming that the Spirit works through small steps.
- Routine, repetitive duties should not be despised because God remains actively faithful in them.
- Walking the path of mundane faithfulness exposes our vulnerabilities and invites God's transforming grace.
